subject: In 2020, Mexico World Cup goal scorer Raúl Jiménez was lying on the turf of the Arsenal Stadium receiving oxygen after fracturing his skull and injuring his brain.
posts:

Evidence: catastrophic injury, medical intervention, athletic return

Raúl Jiménez suffered a severe skull fracture in 2020 during a match. His return to professional football and subsequent goal-scoring performance in the 2026 World Cup is a significant narrative of recovery.

The Poison:
The high-contact nature of professional football continues to pose significant risks to player health, often treated as an acceptable cost of the spectacle.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
There is no plane error here; the event is a straightforward narrative of physical trauma and recovery. The WHY is the athlete's own drive to return to the game.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between the initial catastrophic injury and the eventual return to the World Cup stage...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. The athlete's will to recover creates a positive shift in the probability of his future.

The Unavoidable Truth: Resilience is not the absence of injury, but the ability to continue despite it.

The Unavoidable Lie: That professional sports are purely about the glory of the goal, ignoring the physical toll on the human body.
